title: C# Questions & Answers - Introduction of Reflections
sourceFile: Reflections Basics - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# MCQs focuses on introduction of reflections in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: Which feature enables to obtain information about the use and capabilities of types at runtime?
questions.explanation: Reflection lets you inspect (and often invoke) types, members, and assemblies at runtime. A System.Type object describes the type it represents. Attributes store metadata; they are read through reflection, but they are not the inspection mechanism itself.

questions.question: Choose the namespace which consists of classes that are part of .NET Reflection API?
questions.explanation: Most reflection types (Assembly, MethodInfo, FieldInfo, BindingFlags, and so on) live in System.Reflection. System.Type itself is in System, but it is the entry point to that API.

questions.question: Choose the correct statement about System.Type.

options.text: Core of the reflection subsystem as it encapsulates a type
Consists of many methods and properties that can be used to obtain information about a type at runtime
Both Core of the reflection subsystem as it encapsulates a type & Consists of many methods and properties that can be used to obtain information about a type at runtime
Only Consists of many methods and properties that can be used to obtain information about a type at runtime

questions.explanation: System.Type is a class (not a namespace). It represents a type and exposes members such as GetMethods, GetFields, IsClass, and FullName that you use at runtime.

questions.question: Choose the class from which System.Type is derived?
questions.explanation: Type derives from the abstract class MemberInfo (System.Reflection.MemberInfo). System.Reflection is a namespace, not a base class.

questions.question: What does the following property signify?

options.text: Helps in distinguishing kinds of members
Property helps in determining if member is a field, method, property or event
Both Helps in distinguishing kinds of members & Property helps in determining if member is a field, method, property or event

questions.explanation: MemberInfo.MemberType returns a MemberTypes value (Constructor, Event, Field, Method, Property, NestedType, and others), so you can tell what kind of member you have.

questions.question: Which property obtains a Module object that represents the module (an executable file) in which the reflected type resides?
questions.explanation: MemberInfo.Module (and Type.Module) returns the Module that contains the member or type. DeclaringType is the type that declared the member; ReflectedType is the type used to retrieve it.

questions.question: Choose the method defined by MemberInfo.
questions.explanation: MemberInfo defines GetCustomAttributes, IsDefined, and GetCustomAttributesData. They inspect custom attributes on the member. (The original option spelled GetCustomeAttributesData, which is not a real method.)

questions.question: What does the following declaration specify?

options.text: Returns an array of MethodInfo objects
Returns a list of the public methods supported by the type by using GetMethods()
Both Returns an array of MethodInfo objects & Returns a list of the public methods supported by the type by using GetMethods()

questions.explanation: Type.GetMethods() with no arguments returns the public methods of the type as MethodInfo[]. Other overloads take BindingFlags to include non-public or static members.

questions.question: What does the following C# code specify?

options.text: Any arguments that need to be passed to the method are specified in the array parameters
The value returned by the invoked method is returned by Invoke()

questions.explanation: MethodInfo.Invoke(obj, parameters) calls the method on obj (pass null for a static method). arguments go in parameters (null if none). The boxed return value is what Invoke returns (null for void).

questions.question: What does the following C# method specify?

options.text: Obtains a list of the type arguments bound to a closed constructed generic type
The list may contain both type arguments and type parameters

questions.explanation: Type.GetGenericArguments() is a method on Type, not a MemberInfo property. For a closed constructed type it returns the type arguments (for example string in List<string>). For an open or generic type definition the array can include generic parameters.
